title: Describing people
description: Say what a person is like, and make the adjective match.
grammar: adjectives that change, and ser for what someone is like
grammarNote: An adjective that describes a person goes after ser, and it changes its ending to match.

explanation.summary: These adjectives describe what somebody is like, not how they are at the moment. They go after ser, and they change their ending for the person they describe.

sections.heading: The adjectives
sections.body: Alto, gordo, delgado, guapo, simpático, inteligente, divertido, serio, bonito and feo. The feminine is the same word with -a instead of -o: el simpático is un hombre simpático, la simpática is una mujer simpática. Guapo and feo change in the same way.

sections.heading: With ser, not estar
sections.body: What somebody is like is ser: es alto, es simpático. What somebody is like at this moment is estar: está alto, está cansado. A person is usually described with ser, because being tall or being friendly is part of what they are.

items.note: The feminine is alta: es alta.
The feminine is guapa: mi hermana es guapa.
The feminine is simpática. The accent marks the stress.
The same in both genders: es inteligente.

drills.note: The feminine of simpático is simpática.
The feminine of divertido es divertida.
